subject: Capacity tier rebalance + amendment redline handoff
messages:
From: Micah Torres <micah@cumulusai.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@cumulusai.com
Date: 2026-07-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: add 60 dedicated GPUs + fee consolidation

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the Dedicated pool performance looks great. Our engineering leads confirmed they need an additional 60 GPUs to keep up with customer demand for the next 12 months. We want to: 1) add 60 GPUs to our existing Dedicated Commitment, 2) fold the burst credits into the base commitment (to simplify billing), and 3) lock in the current unit rate for the first 6 months of the amendment.

I've attached a redline (Cumulus_Amendment_v2_redlines.docx) that our procurement team prepared. Can Redwood legal review and propose any language changes? We would like to move quickly — target signing by end of month.

Micah Torres
Head of Infrastructure, CumulusAI
micah@cumulusai.com
+1 415-555-0129

Attachments: Cumulus_Amendment_v2_redlines.docx

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Micah Torres <micah@cumulusai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: add 60 dedicated GPUs + fee consolidation

Micah — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. We're happy to support the capacity increase and the billing consolidation, but we'll need legal to validate a few items in your doc: redlines to the termination/rollback language for phased scaling, the fixed-unit rate term length, and a clear definition of how burst credits convert to committed units.

I've looped in Karthik (customer lead) and Laura (legal) to coordinate. Quick asks from our side to speed review:
- Can you confirm the expected start date for the added GPUs?
- Do you expect a steady consumption profile or a ramp (weeks/months)?
- Are there any export/compliance constraints for workloads?

I'll follow up with a proposed playbook for amendment redlines and a doc sign timeline once legal weighs in.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Micah Torres <micah@cumulusai.com>, contracts@cumulusai.com
Date: 2026-07-16T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: add 60 dedicated GPUs + fee consolidation

Irene / Karthik — reviewing the redline now. Initial legal notes (high-level):
1) Term/Rate Cap: We can agree to lock the current unit rate for 6 months, but need a clause that allows re-pricing after 6 months if wholesale GPU pricing materially changes (define a 15% threshold and notice window).
2) Phased Scale & Rollback: The redline lacks explicit rollback mechanics if utilization falls below a threshold. Propose a 30-day usage lookback and a phased ramp-down with a 90-day notice to align with our capacity planning.
3) Burst Credit Conversion: Instead of an automatic one-to-one conversion to committed units, suggest a weighted conversion table (see cost workbook) tied to 30/60/90-day consumption windows.
4) SLAs & Latency Zones: Add an exhibit that calls out per-region latency targets for the dedicated pool (APIs in us-west only for this commit unless otherwise requested).

I'm attaching a small cost workbook (Cost_Workbook_Q3.xlsx) and will produce a tracked-change version of our preferred amendment language by Monday.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: Cost_Workbook_Q3.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Micah Torres <micah@cumulusai.com>, irene_choi@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-17T11:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Request: add 60 dedicated GPUs + fee consolidation

Micah — quick context from the account team: Cumulus' production window is expected to start 2026-09-01; they anticipate a 6-week ramp to full use (mostly inference traffic, steady qps). Given that profile, the 6-month rate hold is reasonable. Two things on our end:
- Implementation window: We can provision an initial 30 GPUs immediately (pilot cluster) and the remaining 30 in a phased rollout over 45 days. That maps to Laura's phased ramp/rollback asks.
- Commercial: If we accept a weighted conversion, we should include a one-time implementation fee to cover provisioning and guaranteed capacity hold. Suggest $12,500 one-time.

If Cumulus approves the phased provisioning and the one-time fee, Laura and I will align on tracked language for the amendment and route to DocuSign.

Thanks — Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Micah Torres <micah@cumulusai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-19T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: RE: Request: add 60 dedicated GPUs + fee consolidation

Team — appreciate the fast turnaround. Answers below and next steps:
- Start date: target 2026-09-01 for production; pilot (30 GPUs) as soon as provisioning is ready — ideally mid-August.
- Ramp: approx 6 weeks to reach steady state; predictable weekly increases.
- Compliance: no export restrictions for these workloads.

We accept the phased provisioning plan and the $12,500 implementation fee. We also accept the 6-month rate hold with a reasonable re-price clause tied to your 15% wholesale threshold. Please send the tracked-change amendment and the DocuSign link; once our procurement signs, we need provisioning scheduled within 5 business days.

Micah
